data.one_liner: Create and manage multiple windows on desktop platforms in Flutter.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter desktop applications to spawn, manage, and communicate between multiple independent native windows. Each window runs on its own dedicated Flutter engine and isolate.
use_when: Your desktop application needs multi-window support or secondary pop-out windows.
You need bidirectional communication between different application windows.
avoid_when: You are building a mobile or web application.
You only need simple multi-screen routing within a single window.
strengths: Enables true multi-window architecture on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
Provides inter-window communication via method channels.
Supports custom window configurations and arguments.
weaknesses: Plugins must be manually registered for each new window due to separate engine instances.
Requires modifying native project files on Windows, macOS, and Linux for full plugin support.
data.setup_notes: Requires native configuration updates in windows/runner/flutter_window.cpp, macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift, and linux/my_application.cc to register plugins on newly created windows.
